Reference / encoding/base85

encoding/base85#

Strict Base85 codecs with two genuinely implemented variants.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
!#$%&()*+-;<=>?@^_`{|}~

Description#

Strict Base85 codecs with two genuinely implemented variants.

ascii85 uses the contiguous ! through u alphabet. It emits and accepts z for a complete four-zero-byte group, but rejects Adobe <~ ~> wrappers, whitespace and the nonstandard y abbreviation.

rfc1924 uses this exact alphabet:

Both variants encode four bytes as five characters. A final one-, two- or three-byte input group becomes two, three or four characters. A single trailing encoded character is invalid. Decoding rejects values above 0xFFFFFFFF and noncanonical partial groups. InvalidBase85.offset() is a Unicode-scalar offset in encoded input.

Z85 is deliberately absent: its fixed 4-byte/5-character block contract would make encoding partial and deserves a separate consumer-driven API.
